property_summary: After calling owned() as the current owner, the reference contract sets owner to address(0) via transferOwnership(address(0)), while the buggy contract sets owner to address(0) regardless of the argument, so the final owner is the same — this scenario does not diverge. A better scenario: transferOwnership is called with newOwner = address(0x123) by the owner, then owned() is called; the reference keeps owner as address(0x123), the bug sets owner to address(0).

After deploying C with owner=address(this), calling transferOwnership with a new owner, then calling owned() by the original owner, the reference reverts because the modifier checks msg.sender vs owner, while the bug does not revert and owned() succeeds; the divergence is the revert boolean of owned().

Deploy C with deployer as owner, then transfer ownership to another account, then call owned() from the original deployer; the reference reverts because of modifier check, the buggy version does not revert — divergence is revert boolean of owned().
After deployment (owner = address(this)), call owned() from a non-owner address (address(1)); reference reverts due to modifier check but buggy version does not revert.

After deploying C with owner initially 0x0 (address(0)), calling owned() as a non-owner succeeds on the buggy version (require(msg.sender != owner) passes) but reverts in the reference version (require(msg.sender == owner) fails); the observable divergence is whether the call reverts.
